01 / PLANNER

Break the task into a scoped plan. Human approval comes before implementation.

LOCAL PROJECT + GITDURABLE STATE / SQLITEREMOTE CONTROL PLANE ↗

The problem

AI development tools often move the workspace and execution into hosted infrastructure. RLB explores an engineering organization that operates where the developer’s code already lives.

Who it is for

Developers who want supervised agent workflows with local execution and remote visibility.

Engineering challenge

Separate remote control from execution ownership. Preserve approvals, workflow state, and recovery on the local machine while exposing selected events to the cloud.

Architecture

  1. Electron desktop → local FastAPI runtime
  2. Durable worker → specialized agents → staging → approval
  3. Local project + Git + SQLite durable state
  4. Outbound connection → cloud control plane → web console

Simplified architecture based on repository documentation.

Technology choices

  • Python
  • FastAPI
  • Electron
  • SQLite
  • Git

The stack above is documented in the repository. The architecture separates interface, execution or business logic, and persistence.

Documented implementation

  • Durable approval and recovery state
  • Authenticated device pairing and remote commands
  • Event catch-up and private review artifacts
  • Staging, promotion, testing, and review workflows

Current limits

The Windows-first implementation is undergoing an architecture transition. Windows installer acceptance and live hosted account/deployment acceptance still require external environments. Local deterministic checks do not certify those deployments.

Design takeaway

Local-first architecture is an ownership decision: remote visibility does not require relocating the codebase.

This is an architectural interpretation of the documented implementation, not a measured outcome or a personal claim.
